---
name: $name
description: $description
---

# $venue: submission format check

Checks a paper against the $venue author kit (rules extracted on $date) and reports what to fix, where, and how.
The rules live in `rules.json`; the checking code in `scripts/` is generic. Every rule keeps a pointer to the kit passage it came from, so a
wrong rule can be traced and corrected instead of trusted blindly.

## Workflow

1. **Collect inputs.** The normal case is that the user uploads the **whole paper folder** (or a zip of it). Use project mode; it needs nothing else:
   it finds the main .tex, picks the paper PDF (not the figure PDFs), compiles a copy if there is no PDF, warns when the PDF is older than the sources,
   checks every `\includegraphics` (missing files, non-embedded/Type 3 fonts, per figure) and scans the whole folder for identity leaks (`.git`, .bib, aux/fls paths).
   If only a PDF or only a .docx is given, run the narrower checks and say which checks could not run.
   Also establish the **phase**: $phases_line If the user does not say, ask once; the rules differ (anonymity, line numbers, page limit).
   For anonymity checks ask for the author names / institutions to search for (`--names "A,B,Univ X"`); they are used only for this run.
2. **Compilation.** Project mode compiles a copy when no paper PDF is in the folder. If compilation fails, the report shows the log tail; fix the
   first error. Never "fix" a compile error by editing the official style file. A PDF the user compiled themselves is preferable to ours if their
   TeX distribution differs (page breaks can shift slightly), so mention which PDF was checked.
3. **Run the engine** (from this skill's folder):
   ```
   python scripts/run_checks.py --rules rules.json --project PAPER_FOLDER_OR_ZIP \
       --phase $default_phase --names "..." --out report.md --json report.json
   ```
   Add `--main sub/paper.tex` if the folder has several files with `\documentclass` (the report says which one it picked; confirm it with the user
   when it is ambiguous). Uploaded folders are read-only: the checker never edits them and compiles only a copy. Without a project folder use
   `--pdf PAPER.pdf` and/or `--tex SOURCE`.
   Exit code 1 means at least one must-fix finding. `--docx FILE [--docx-to-pdf]` handles Word files.
4. **Handle the manual checklist.** Items marked as manual need your judgement: read the relevant part of the paper (PDF text or source) and decide
   pass / fail / unsure, quoting the evidence (section name, one sentence). Never mark a manual item as passed without having looked.
5. **Report to the user** in the user's language, ordered by risk of desk rejection: must-fix first, then warnings, then manual items.
   For each problem give the location (file:line or page), why it matters (one clause), and the concrete fix. For LaTeX fixes, show the exact
   lines to change. Offer to apply the fixes to a copy of the source, recompile, and re-run the engine until no must-fix remains.
6. **Close honestly.** State which inputs were not provided (so which checks did not run) and remind the user that the official CFP/kit
   is the authority; the submission system may apply additional automatic checks.

## What the rules cover

$rule_summary

Details and the original wording of each rule: `references/kit_notes.md` (if present) and the `_sources` fields in `rules.json`.

## Known blind spots (say so when relevant)

- Text-extraction based checks (headings, anonymity, checklist keywords) can miss text inside figures and can misread unusual layouts.
- Page-limit logic assumes the main body ends at the first heading listed in `pdf.page_limit.main_body_ends_at`; check by eye if the paper uses unusual section names.
- Margin checks inspect words and embedded images, not vector drawings; a wide TikZ/vector figure can still overflow.
- Word files: Word does not store page breaks, so page count needs a PDF export.
- Style-file integrity is only verifiable when the style files are inside the project folder.
- Compliance with this checker is not a guarantee against desk rejection.

## Updating this skill

Venues revise their kits yearly. When a new author kit is released, regenerate this skill from it (or edit `rules.json` and replace `assets/official/`)
rather than patching individual rules from memory.

# Inkwell integration

Source: the user-supplied `venue-checker-factory.skill` archive (2026-10-18).
Rebuild its offline snapshot with `node scripts/bundle-venue-factory.mjs`.

The format builder supplies SKILL.md and the rules schema to the selected model.
It collects clarification answers, verifies literal source quotes, previews the
rules and packages the generic engine after confirmation. Machine-rule sources
use preview rule IDs during generation; Inkwell resolves them to original quotes.
Recommendations and checks that cannot be encoded faithfully remain manual items.
Official style copies keep the uploaded text; their hashes normalize CRLF exactly
as the Python engine does. Importing scripts stores text and never executes them.

The desktop builder uses its existing PDF parser and author-kit ZIP reader in
place of extract_kit.py. It assembles the skill in Node without requiring Python
or Claude-specific directories, package_skill, or present_files. Existing saved
skills stay available; newly generated skills use this factory.

Local engine changes: absent forbid_layout_hacks and require_embedded flags now
default to false. The kit must explicitly require those checks. The upstream
factory workflow, schema, builder and extraction scripts are retained as reference.

Calibration is not part of text-only extraction. Generated skills and the preview
state that official-sample and mutation controls have not run. The built-in Agent
can execute the enabled skill's verified script with run_python in ask/auto modes.
Restricted mode disables Python. Missing interpreters, dependencies or unperformed
checks must be reported as NOT VERIFIED. External Agents with execution tools can
also materialize declared resources and run the engine.
Python dependencies and TeX/LibreOffice availability are separate
from Skill generation; the application does not install them automatically.

# rules.json schema

Fill only what the kit actually states. A missing key means "do not check"; never guess a value from memory of what this venue "usually" requires,
because a wrong rule produces false alarms that teach the user to ignore the report. Every block carries `_sources`: a short pointer to the kit
passage (file, page or section, plus a few words of the original) for each rule, so a human can verify it in seconds.

Units: lengths in `margins` use `unit` (`in`, `cm`, `mm`, `pt`). Sizes are in pt.

```jsonc
{
  "venue": "ACL 2027",                 // shown in the report title
  "default_phase": "review",           // phase used when --phase is not given
  "phases": {                          // overrides deep-merged on top of the base rules
    "review": {"anonymity": {"required": true}, "pdf": {"line_numbers": "required"}},
    "final":  {"anonymity": {"required": false}, "pdf": {"line_numbers": "forbidden", "page_limit": {"main_body": 9}}}
  },

  "pdf": {                             // checks on the compiled PDF
    "page_size": "A4",                 // "A4" | "Letter"
    "page_limit": {
      "main_body": 8,                  // pages of content that count
      "total": null,                   // hard cap on all pages, if the kit has one
      "main_body_ends_at": ["Limitations", "Ethics.*", "References"]   // regexes for heading lines that end the counted part
    },
    "margins": {"unit": "cm", "top": 2.5, "bottom": 2.5, "left": 2.5, "right": 2.5,
                "tolerance_pt": 3, "skip_top_pt": 0, "skip_bottom_pt": 0},
    "fonts": {
      "allowed_families": ["Times", "NimbusRom"],   // substrings, case/punctuation-insensitive; math fonts are always allowed
      "body_size_pt": 11, "min_size_pt": 8,
      "require_embedded": true, "forbid_type3": false
    },
    "line_numbers": "required",        // "required" | "forbidden" | null
    "_sources": {"page_size": "...", "page_limit": "...", "margins": "...", "fonts": "...", "line_numbers": "..."}
  },

  "tex": {                             // checks on the LaTeX source
    "documentclass": {"name": "article", "options_required": ["11pt"], "options_forbidden": []},
    "packages_required": [{"name": "acl", "options_required": ["review"], "options_forbidden": ["final"]}],
    "packages_forbidden": ["geometry"],         // omit to use the default list (savetrees, fullpage, setspace, titlesec)
    "allow_packages": [],                       // exempt from the forbidden list (e.g. the template itself loads geometry)
    "forbid_layout_hacks": true,                // negative \vspace, \baselinestretch, \setlength{\textwidth}, \geometry ...
    "layout_hacks_severity": "warn",            // "error" if the kit says deviations are rejected
    "bibliography_style": ["acl_natbib"],
    "official_files": {"acl.sty": {}, "acl_natbib.bst": {}},   // hashes are filled in from the kit by build_venue_skill.py
    "_sources": {"documentclass": "...", "packages_required": "...", "official_files": "..."}
  },

  "docx": {                            // Word submissions
    "page_size": "Letter", "margins": {"unit": "in", "top": 1, "bottom": 1, "left": 1, "right": 1},
    "fonts": {"allowed_families": ["Times New Roman"], "body_size_pt": 10},
    "line_spacing": 1.0, "page_limit": 6,
    "_sources": {}
  },

  "anonymity": {                       // applies to PDF and source when required
    "required": true,
    "forbid_text_patterns": ["our (previous|prior) work"],     // optional extra regexes
    "forbid_headings": ["Acknowledg(e)?ments?"],
    "_sources": {"required": "..."}
  },

  "checklist": [                       // content requirements the kit imposes
    {
      "id": "limitations",             // short slug, unique
      "title": "Limitations section",
      "severity": "error",             // "error" | "warn"  (error = the kit says missing => desk reject)
      "source": "kit/acl_cfp.pdf p.3: 'papers without a Limitations section will be desk rejected'",
      "description": "what a human/LLM must verify; used for manual items",
      "needs_judgement": false,        // true: even when detected, still list as a manual check
      "detect": [                      // tried in order; first applicable one wins
        {"type": "tex_section", "title_regex": "Limitations", "min_words": 40},
        {"type": "pdf_regex", "patterns": ["^\\s*(\\d+\\s+)?Limitations\\s*$"]}
      ],
      "fix": "Add \\section*{Limitations} after the conclusion (does not count toward the page limit)."
    }
  ]
}
```

`detect` types: `tex_section` (title regex + minimum words, approximate), `tex_regex` (patterns searched in the comment-stripped source),
`pdf_regex` (patterns searched in the PDF text; `^`/`$` work per line). Add `"expect": "absent"` to a regex detector to require that
something is NOT present. Items without `detect`, or whose input type was not supplied, become manual checks.

## Translating kit language into rules

| Kit says | Put in rules |
|---|---|
| "8 pages of content, unlimited references" | `page_limit.main_body: 8`, `main_body_ends_at: ["References"]` |
| "Limitations/Ethics sections do not count" | add their headings to `main_body_ends_at` **and** a checklist item if mandatory |
| "text area 6.75 x 9 in on Letter" | margins: `(8.5-6.75)/2 = 0.875` left/right; `(11-9)/2 = 1.0` top/bottom, `unit: "in"` (say in `_sources` that it was derived) |
| "Times New Roman 10pt" | `fonts.allowed_families: ["Times","NimbusRom"]` (LaTeX `times`/`newtx` render as Nimbus), `body_size_pt: 10` |
| "all fonts must be Type 1 / embedded" | `require_embedded: true`, `forbid_type3: true` |
| "do not modify the style file / margins / spacing" | `official_files` for each .sty/.cls/.bst, `forbid_layout_hacks: true`, `layout_hacks_severity: "error"` |
| "submissions must be anonymous" | phase `review`: `anonymity.required: true` (+ review option in `packages_required`) |
| "include a reproducibility / responsible-NLP checklist" | checklist item, `severity: "error"`, usually manual unless the checklist is a fixed .tex block you can regex |
| "should", "recommended", "encouraged" | `severity: "warn"` |
| "must", "will be rejected", "required" | `severity: "error"` |

## Traps

- Review and camera-ready kits differ (page limit +1, no line numbers, authors shown). Always model phases; ask the user which one they are submitting.
- Different tracks (long/short/demo, main/industry) have different limits: ask which track, or build one skill per track by passing `--name` suffixes.
- If the LaTeX style file is the ground truth (e.g. it computes `\textwidth`), prefer `official_files` + the compiled-PDF checks over re-deriving numbers by hand.
- When the PDF kit and the style file disagree, trust the style file for geometry and the PDF for policy, and note the conflict in `kit_notes.md`.
- Heading regexes in `main_body_ends_at` match a whole line, so `"References"` will not match `"References and Notes"`; list variants.

"""Word (.docx) checks. Layout-dependent rules (page count) need a PDF export: see run_checks --docx-to-pdf."""
import re
from collections import Counter

from docx import Document

from .common import finding, margins_pt, sources, Finding

PAGE_SIZES = {"A4": (595.28, 841.89), "LETTER": (612.0, 792.0)}


def _norm(s):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", (s or "").lower())


def run(path, rules, names=None):
    D = rules.get("docx", {}) or {}
    S = sources(D)
    F = []
    doc = Document(path)
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    ctx = {"text": "\n".join(p.text for p in doc.paragraphs)}

    if D.get("page_size"):
        want = PAGE_SIZES[D["page_size"].upper()]
        w, h = sec.page_width.pt, sec.page_height.pt
        ok = abs(w - want[0]) <= 3 and abs(h - want[1]) <= 3
        F.append(finding("docx.page_size", ok, f"Page size is {D['page_size']}", f"Document is {w:.0f}x{h:.0f} pt",
                         fix="Layout > Size > choose the required paper size.", source=S.get("page_size", "")))

    M = margins_pt(D.get("margins"))
    if M:
        tol = float((D.get("margins") or {}).get("tolerance_pt", 3))
        have = {"top": sec.top_margin.pt, "bottom": sec.bottom_margin.pt,
                "left": sec.left_margin.pt, "right": sec.right_margin.pt}
        bad = [f"{k}: {have[k]:.0f}pt vs required {v:.0f}pt" for k, v in M.items() if abs(have[k] - v) > tol]
        F.append(finding("docx.margins", not bad, "Margins match the requirement", "; ".join(bad),
                         fix="Layout > Margins > Custom Margins, enter the values from the kit.",
                         source=S.get("margins", "")))

    # fonts: count characters per (font, size), falling back to the style / Normal defaults
    normal = doc.styles["Normal"].font
    cnt_font, cnt_size = Counter(), Counter()
    spacing = Counter()
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if not p.text.strip():
            continue
        pf = p.style.font if p.style is not None else None
        spacing[p.paragraph_format.line_spacing or (p.style.paragraph_format.line_spacing if p.style is not None else None)] += len(p.text)
        for r in p.runs:
            n = len(r.text.strip())
            if not n:
                continue
            name = r.font.name or (pf.name if pf is not None else None) or normal.name
            size = r.font.size or (pf.size if pf is not None else None) or normal.size
            cnt_font[name] += n
            cnt_size[round(size.pt, 1) if size else None] += n
    FO = D.get("fonts") or {}
    allowed = [_norm(a) for a in FO.get("allowed_families", [])]
    if allowed:
        bad = {f: c for f, c in cnt_font.items() if not any(a in _norm(f) for a in allowed)}
        F.append(finding("docx.fonts_allowed", not bad, "Only the required font family is used",
                         "" if not bad else "Other fonts: " + ", ".join(f"{f or 'default'} ({c} chars)" for f, c in bad.items()),
                         fix="Select all (Ctrl+A) and set the font from the kit; check headings, captions and tables.",
                         source=S.get("fonts", "")))
    if FO.get("body_size_pt"):
        dom = cnt_size.most_common(1)[0][0] if cnt_size else None
        F.append(finding("docx.font_size_body", dom is not None and abs(dom - FO["body_size_pt"]) <= 0.35,
                         f"Body text is {FO['body_size_pt']} pt", f"Most common size: {dom} pt",
                         fix="Set the Normal style to the required size instead of formatting runs by hand.",
                         source=S.get("fonts", "")))
    if D.get("line_spacing") is not None:
        dom = spacing.most_common(1)[0][0] if spacing else None
        F.append(finding("docx.line_spacing", dom is not None and abs(float(dom) - D["line_spacing"]) <= 0.05,
                         f"Line spacing is {D['line_spacing']}", f"Dominant line spacing: {dom}",
                         fix="Paragraph > Line spacing: set the value from the kit.", source=S.get("line_spacing", "")))
    if D.get("page_limit"):
        F.append(Finding("docx.page_limit", "manual", f"Page limit ({D['page_limit']})",
                         "Word does not store page breaks reliably. Re-run with --docx-to-pdf (LibreOffice) or export to PDF "
                         "from Word and pass --pdf. Remember the PDF produced by LibreOffice may differ slightly from Word."))
    return F, ctx

"""PDF checks (pdfplumber + poppler's pdffonts)."""
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

import pdfplumber

from .common import finding, margins_pt, sources, Finding

PAGE_SIZES = {"A4": (595.28, 841.89), "LETTER": (612.0, 792.0)}
# pdfplumber merges glyphs closer than x_tolerance; its default (3pt) swallows the narrow word spaces of Times
# ("Wei Feng" -> "WeiFeng"), which silently breaks every text match. 1.2pt keeps words apart and kerning intact.
XTOL = 1.2
# Math / symbol fonts are expected even when the text font is restricted.
MATH_FONT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(CMMI|CMSY|CMEX|CMBSY|CMMIB|MSAM|MSBM|LMMath|STIX|TXMI|TXSY|TXEX|MTMI|MTSY|MTEX|MTExtra|"
    r"rsfs|EUFM|EUSM|EURM|EURB|Symbol|ZapfDingbats|Wasy|lasy)", re.I)
EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+(?:\.[\w-]+)+")
HOST_RE = re.compile(r"(?:github\.com|gitlab\.com|bitbucket\.org|huggingface\.co|sites\.google\.com|"
                     r"\w+\.github\.io)/?[\w./-]*", re.I)


def _norm(s):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", (s or "").lower())


def _strip_subset(name):
    return re.sub(r"^[A-Z]{6}\+", "", name or "")


def split_lines(words, gap=14.0, ytol=2.5):
    """Group words into visual lines, splitting at column gaps."""
    rows = []
    for w in sorted(words, key=lambda w: (w["top"], w["x0"])):
        for r in rows:
            if abs(r[0]["top"] - w["top"]) <= ytol:
                r.append(w)
                break
        else:
            rows.append([w])
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        r.sort(key=lambda w: w["x0"])
        seg = [r[0]]
        for w in r[1:]:
            if w["x0"] - seg[-1]["x1"] > gap:
                out.append(seg)
                seg = [w]
            else:
                seg.append(w)
        out.append(seg)
    return [{"text": " ".join(w["text"] for w in s), "x0": s[0]["x0"], "x1": s[-1]["x1"],
             "top": min(w["top"] for w in s), "bottom": max(w["bottom"] for w in s)} for s in out]


def _heading_matches(text, patterns):
    cands = {text.strip(), re.sub(r"^(?:[A-Z]|\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\.?\s+", "", text.strip())}
    return any(re.fullmatch(p, c, re.I) for p in patterns for c in cands)


def _pdffonts(path):
    exe = shutil.which("pdffonts")
    if not exe:
        return None
    try:
        out = subprocess.run([exe, path], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60).stdout
    except Exception:
        return None
    rows = []
    for line in out.splitlines()[2:]:
        m = re.match(r"^(\S+)\s+(.+?)\s+(yes|no)\s+(yes|no)\s+(yes|no)\s+\d+\s+\d+\s*$", line)
        if m:
            rows.append({"name": _strip_subset(m.group(1)), "type": m.group(2), "emb": m.group(3) == "yes"})
    return rows


def run(pdf_path, rules, names=None):
    P = rules.get("pdf", {}) or {}
    S = sources(P)
    names = names or []
    F = []
    ctx = {}
    with pdfplumber.open(pdf_path) as pdf:
        pages = pdf.pages
        n = len(pages)
        words_by_page = [p.extract_words(use_text_flow=False, keep_blank_chars=False, x_tolerance=XTOL, extra_attrs=["size"]) for p in pages]
        text_pages = [p.extract_text(x_tolerance=XTOL) or "" for p in pages]
        ctx["text"] = "\n".join(text_pages)
        ctx["pages_text"] = text_pages
        meta = pdf.metadata or {}

        # ---- page size -------------------------------------------------
        if P.get("page_size"):
            want = PAGE_SIZES[P["page_size"].upper()]
            bad = [i + 1 for i, p in enumerate(pages)
                   if abs(p.width - want[0]) > 3 or abs(p.height - want[1]) > 3]
            F.append(finding("pdf.page_size", not bad, f"Page size is {P['page_size']}",
                             "" if not bad else f"Pages with wrong size: {bad[:10]} (first page is "
                             f"{pages[0].width:.0f}x{pages[0].height:.0f} pt)",
                             fix="Set the paper size from the official style file (e.g. `\\usepackage[a4paper]{...}` "
                                 "or the template's own option). Do not hand-set `\\paperwidth`; also check "
                                 "`dvips/dvipdf` or `\\pdfpagewidth` settings if you compile via DVI.",
                             source=S.get("page_size", "")))

        # ---- page limits -----------------------------------------------
        PL = P.get("page_limit") or {}
        if PL.get("total") is not None:
            F.append(finding("pdf.total_pages", n <= PL["total"], f"Total pages <= {PL['total']}",
                             f"PDF has {n} pages", fix="Cut content or move material to an allowed appendix.",
                             source=S.get("page_limit", "")))
        if PL.get("main_body") is not None:
            limit = PL["main_body"]
            markers = PL.get("main_body_ends_at") or []
            hit = None
            for i, (p, words) in enumerate(zip(pages, words_by_page)):
                for ln in split_lines(words):
                    if _heading_matches(ln["text"], markers):
                        hit = (i, ln, p)
                        break
                if hit:
                    break
            if not markers or not hit:
                F.append(finding("pdf.page_limit", n <= limit,
                                 f"Main body <= {limit} pages",
                                 f"Could not locate a heading that ends the main body (looked for {markers}). "
                                 f"PDF has {n} pages in total, so the main body is at most {n}. "
                                 "Verify the page where References/Limitations start by hand.",
                                 severity="warn" if n > limit else "error",
                                 fix="Cut content so the main text fits; sections the kit excludes from the limit "
                                     "(references, limitations, ethics...) may spill over.",
                                 source=S.get("page_limit", "")))
            else:
                i, ln, p = hit
                pno = i + 1
                note = ""
                ok = pno <= limit
                if not ok and pno == limit + 1:
                    above = [w for w in words_by_page[i]
                             if w["top"] < ln["top"] - 3 and w["top"] > 0.07 * p.height
                             and not re.fullmatch(r"[\d.,:]+", w["text"])]
                    if not above:
                        ok = True
                        note = " (the excluded section starts at the very top of the next page, so the body ends on the limit page)"
                F.append(finding("pdf.page_limit", ok, f"Main body <= {limit} pages",
                                 f"Main body ends where heading '{ln['text']}' starts: page {pno}, "
                                 f"{100 * ln['top'] / p.height:.0f}% down the page{note}.",
                                 location=f"page {pno}",
                                 fix=f"Cut {'roughly a page or more' if pno > limit + 1 else 'part of a page'} of body text "
                                     "before that heading: shrink figures, trim related work, move detail to the appendix "
                                     "if the venue allows. Do not use negative \\vspace.",
                                 source=S.get("page_limit", "")))

        # ---- margins ---------------------------------------------------
        M = margins_pt(P.get("margins"))
        if M and len(M) == 4:
            tol = float((P.get("margins") or {}).get("tolerance_pt", 3))
            skip_top = float((P.get("margins") or {}).get("skip_top_pt", 0))
            skip_bot = float((P.get("margins") or {}).get("skip_bottom_pt", 0))
            viol = defaultdict(dict)   # page -> side -> (overflow, sample)
            for i, (p, words) in enumerate(zip(pages, words_by_page), 1):
                W, H = p.width, p.height
                L, R, T, B = M["left"], W - M["right"], M["top"], H - M["bottom"]
                items = []
                for w in words:
                    if w["bottom"] < skip_top or w["top"] > H - skip_bot:
                        continue
                    outside = w["x1"] < L or w["x0"] > R or w["bottom"] < T or w["top"] > B
                    if outside and re.fullmatch(r"[\d.,:]+", w["text"]):
                        continue  # line / page numbers living in the margin
                    items.append((w["x0"], w["x1"], w["top"], w["bottom"], w["text"][:30], w.get("size", 10)))
                for im in p.images:
                    items.append((im["x0"], im["x1"], im["top"], im["bottom"], "<image>", 0))
                for x0, x1, top, bot, txt, sz in items:
                    # glyph boxes extend beyond the TeX text block by a fraction of the font size
                    vt = tol + 0.35 * sz
                    for side, over, t_ in (("left", L - x0, tol), ("right", x1 - R, tol),
                                           ("top", T - top, vt), ("bottom", bot - B, vt)):
                        if over > t_ and over > viol[i].get(side, (0, ""))[0]:
                            viol[i][side] = (over, txt)
            detail = "; ".join(f"p{pg}: " + ", ".join(f"{side} +{o:.0f}pt ('{s}')" for side, (o, s) in d.items())
                               for pg, d in list(viol.items())[:6])
            F.append(finding("pdf.margins", not viol, "Content stays inside the required margins",
                             "" if not viol else f"{len(viol)} page(s) overflow: {detail}",
                             location="" if not viol else f"pages {list(viol)[:12]}",
                             fix="Overflow is usually one of: a wide table/figure (`\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{...}` or "
                                 "`tabularx`/`\\small`), a long unbreakable URL or identifier (`\\usepackage{xurl}`, "
                                 "`\\sloppy`, or rephrase), or an overlong equation (`multline`/`split`). "
                                 "Do not edit margins or the style file.",
                             source=S.get("margins", "")))

        # ---- fonts -----------------------------------------------------
        FO = P.get("fonts") or {}
        fam, sizes = Counter(), Counter()
        small = defaultdict(Counter)   # page -> size -> chars
        for i, p in enumerate(pages, 1):
            for ch in p.chars:
                name = _strip_subset(ch.get("fontname", ""))
                if MATH_FONT_RE.match(name) or not ch["text"].strip():
                    continue
                fam[name] += 1
                sizes[round(ch["size"], 1)] += 1
                floor = FO.get("min_size_pt")
                if floor and ch["size"] < floor - 0.25:
                    small[i][round(ch["size"], 1)] += 1
        allowed = [_norm(a) for a in FO.get("allowed_families", [])]
        if allowed:
            bad = {f: c for f, c in fam.items() if c >= FO.get("min_chars_to_flag", 20)
                   and not any(a in _norm(f) for a in allowed)}
            if "unknown" in bad:
                bad["unknown (Type 3 / bitmap font, name unreadable)"] = bad.pop("unknown")
            F.append(finding("pdf.fonts_allowed", not bad, "Only the required font family is used",
                             "" if not bad else "Unexpected fonts (chars): " + ", ".join(f"{f} ({c})" for f, c in
                                                                                         sorted(bad.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:8]),
                             fix="Unreadable names or CM*/Latin Modern text fonts usually mean the required font was not found (TeX then builds bitmap Type 3 fonts), the style file was not loaded, or it was overridden "
                                 "(e.g. a later `\\usepackage{lmodern}`/`\\renewcommand{\\rmdefault}`). Fonts from figures: "
                                 "re-export with the required font; in matplotlib set `rcParams['pdf.fonttype']=42` and "
                                 "`rcParams['font.family']='serif'`.",
                             source=S.get("fonts", "")))
        if FO.get("body_size_pt"):
            dom = sizes.most_common(1)[0][0] if sizes else None
            ok = dom is not None and abs(dom - FO["body_size_pt"]) <= 0.35
            F.append(finding("pdf.font_size_body", ok, f"Body text is {FO['body_size_pt']} pt",
                             f"Most common text size is {dom} pt" if dom else "No text found",
                             fix="Use the size option from the official template (e.g. `[11pt]` in `\\documentclass`); "
                                 "never rescale with `\\fontsize` or `\\small` for the whole document.",
                             source=S.get("fonts", "")))
        if FO.get("min_size_pt"):
            tot = sum(sum(c.values()) for c in small.values())
            thr = FO.get("min_chars_to_flag", 20) * 2
            F.append(finding("pdf.font_size_min", tot < thr, f"No text smaller than {FO['min_size_pt']} pt",
                             "" if tot < thr else f"{tot} characters below the floor, e.g. " +
                             "; ".join(f"p{pg}: " + ", ".join(f"{s}pt x{c}" for s, c in cnt.most_common(2))
                                       for pg, cnt in list(small.items())[:5]),
                             location="" if tot < thr else f"pages {list(small)[:12]}",
                             fix="Usually tiny table text (`\\tiny`, `\\scriptsize`) or text inside figures: "
                                 "enlarge figure fonts to match caption size, split wide tables, or use `\\footnotesize` "
                                 "at the smallest if the kit allows it.",
                             source=S.get("fonts", "")))
        pf = _pdffonts(pdf_path)
        if pf is not None:
            if FO.get("require_embedded", False):
                noemb = sorted({r["name"] for r in pf if not r["emb"]})
                F.append(finding("pdf.fonts_embedded", not noemb, "All fonts are embedded",
                                 "" if not noemb else "Not embedded: " + ", ".join(noemb[:8]),
                                 fix="Figures are the usual culprit. Re-export with embedded fonts (matplotlib: "
                                     "`pdf.fonttype=42`; Illustrator/Inkscape: 'convert text to outlines' or embed all). "
                                     "Then compile with `pdflatex` (not dvips) and check `pdffonts paper.pdf`.",
                                 source=S.get("fonts", "")))
            if FO.get("forbid_type3"):
                t3 = sorted({r["name"] for r in pf if r["type"].lower().startswith("type 3")})
                F.append(finding("pdf.type3", not t3, "No Type 3 fonts",
                                 "" if not t3 else "Type 3 fonts: " + ", ".join(t3[:8]),
                                 fix="Matplotlib: `matplotlib.rcParams['pdf.fonttype']=42` (and `ps.fonttype`). "
                                     "Other tools: export TrueType/Type 1 instead of Type 3. Fix the figure, regenerate, recompile.",
                                 source=S.get("fonts", "")))
        else:
            F.append(Finding("pdf.fonts_embedded", "skip", "Font embedding check skipped",
                             "`pdffonts` (poppler-utils) not found."))

        # ---- line numbers ------------------------------------------------
        ln_rule = P.get("line_numbers")  # "required" | "forbidden" | None
        if ln_rule and M:
            cnt = 0
            for p, words in list(zip(pages, words_by_page))[:2]:
                cnt += sum(1 for w in words if re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,4}", w["text"]) and w["x1"] < M["left"] + 2)
            has = cnt >= 15
            if ln_rule == "required":
                F.append(finding("pdf.line_numbers", has, "Line numbers are present (review version)",
                                 f"Found {cnt} margin numbers on the first two pages",
                                 fix="Enable the review option of the official style (e.g. `\\usepackage[review]{...}`).",
                                 source=S.get("line_numbers", "")))
            else:
                F.append(finding("pdf.line_numbers", not has, "No line numbers (final version)",
                                 f"Found {cnt} margin numbers on the first two pages",
                                 fix="Switch the style option to the final/camera-ready mode.",
                                 source=S.get("line_numbers", "")))

        # ---- anonymity ---------------------------------------------------
        A = rules.get("anonymity") or {}
        if A.get("required"):
            author = (meta.get("Author") or "").strip()
            bad_meta = bool(author) and author.lower() not in ("anonymous", "anonymous authors")
            hits = [n_ for n_ in names if n_ and (n_.lower() in author.lower() or n_.lower() in (meta.get("Title") or "").lower())]
            F.append(finding("pdf.anon_metadata", not (bad_meta or hits), "PDF metadata does not reveal authors",
                             "" if not (bad_meta or hits) else f"PDF Author field is '{author}'",
                             fix="Set `\\hypersetup{pdfauthor={}}` or remove the `pdfauthor` entry from `\\usepackage[...]{hyperref}`; "
                                 "check Title too. Verify with `pdfinfo paper.pdf`.",
                             source=sources(A).get("required", "")))
            pats = [re.compile(p, re.I) for p in A.get("forbid_text_patterns", [])]
            pats += [EMAIL_RE, HOST_RE] + [re.compile(re.escape(x), re.I) for x in names if x]
            leaks = []
            for pi, t in enumerate(text_pages, 1):
                for rx in pats:
                    for m in rx.finditer(t):
                        leaks.append(f"p{pi}: '{m.group(0)[:50]}'")
                squashed = re.sub(r"\s+", "", t).lower()
                for x in names:
                    if x and re.sub(r"\s+", "", x).lower() in squashed and not any(
                            x.lower() in l.lower() for l in leaks if l.startswith(f"p{pi}:")):
                        leaks.append(f"p{pi}: '{x}' (found ignoring spaces)")
            for pi, t in enumerate(text_pages, 1):
                for h in A.get("forbid_headings", [r"Acknowledg(e)?ments?"]):
                    if re.search(rf"^\s*(?:\d+\s+)?{h}\s*$", t, re.I | re.M):
                        leaks.append(f"p{pi}: heading '{h}'")
            F.append(finding("pdf.anon_text", not leaks, "No identifying text in the PDF body",
                             "" if not leaks else "; ".join(leaks[:10]),
                             fix="Remove emails, repository links and acknowledgements for the review version (or replace "
                                 "with anonymous links, e.g. anonymous.4open.science). Cite your own prior work in third person.",
                             source=sources(A).get("required", "")))
    return F, ctx

"""LaTeX source checks. Input: a .tex file, a directory, or a .zip of the project."""
import bisect
import difflib
import re
import tempfile
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from .common import finding, sources, sha256_normalized, Finding

COMMENT_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\\)%.*$")
INPUT_RE = re.compile(r"\\(?:input|include|subfile)\s*\{([^}]+)\}")
USEPKG_RE = re.compile(r"\\(?:usepackage|RequirePackage)\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*\{([^}]*)\}")
DOCCLASS_RE = re.compile(r"\\documentclass\s*(?:\[([^\]]*)\])?\s*\{([^}]*)\}")
EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+(?:\.[\w-]+)+")

# Typical "squeeze the page limit" tricks. Severity is configurable via tex.layout_hacks_severity.
LAYOUT_HACKS = [
    (r"\\vspace\*?\s*\{\s*-", "negative \\vspace (squeezes spacing)",
     "Delete it. If the page limit is the problem, cut text or shrink figures instead."),
    (r"\\vskip\s*-", "negative \\vskip", "Delete it; cut content instead."),
    (r"\\(baselinestretch|linespread|setstretch)", "line spacing override",
     "Remove it; line spacing is fixed by the official style."),
    (r"\\(?:set|add)length\s*\{\s*\\(textwidth|textheight|oddsidemargin|evensidemargin|topmargin|headheight|"
     r"columnsep|parskip|parindent|textfloatsep|floatsep|intextsep|abovecaptionskip|belowcaptionskip|"
     r"abovedisplayskip|belowdisplayskip)\s*\}", "page/spacing length override",
     "Remove it unless the venue explicitly allows adjusting this length."),
    (r"\\fontsize\s*\{", "manual \\fontsize", "Remove it and use the template's size commands."),
    (r"\\(?:geometry|newgeometry)\s*\{", "geometry override", "Remove it; margins come from the official style."),
    (r"\\looseness\s*=?\s*-", "negative \\looseness", "Remove it; rewrite the paragraph if you need to save a line."),
    (r"\\enlargethispage", "\\enlargethispage", "Remove it; it extends the text block."),
    (r"\\(?:titlespacing|titleformat)", "section title spacing override", "Remove it; headings follow the template."),
]
DEFAULT_FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES = ["savetrees", "fullpage", "setspace", "titlesec"]


class Source:
    def __init__(self, path, main=None):
        p = Path(path)
        self.tmp = None
        if p.suffix.lower() == ".zip":
            self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tex_")
            zipfile.ZipFile(p).extractall(self.tmp)
            root = Path(self.tmp)
        elif p.is_dir():
            root = p
        else:
            root = p.parent
        self.root = root
        if main:
            m = Path(main)
            self.main = m if m.is_absolute() else root / m
            if not self.main.is_file():
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"--main {main} not found under {root}")
        else:
            self.main = p if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() == ".tex" else self._find_main(root)
        self.base = self.main.parent
        self.lines = []       # (relpath, lineno, cleaned, raw)
        self._load(self.main, set())
        self.clean = "\n".join(l[2] for l in self.lines)
        self.offsets, off = [], 0
        for l in self.lines:
            self.offsets.append(off)
            off += len(l[2]) + 1

    def _find_main(self, root):
        cands = []
        for f in root.rglob("*.tex"):
            try:
                t = f.read_text(errors="ignore")
            except Exception:
                continue
            if DOCCLASS_RE.search("\n".join(COMMENT_RE.sub("", x) for x in t.splitlines())):
                cands.append(f)
        if not cands:
            raise FileNotFoundError("no .tex file with \\documentclass found")
        pref = [c for c in cands if c.name.lower() in ("main.tex", "paper.tex", "ms.tex", "anonymous.tex")]
        return (pref or sorted(cands, key=lambda c: -c.stat().st_size))[0]

    def _load(self, f, seen):
        if f in seen or not f.exists():
            return
        seen.add(f)
        rel = str(f.relative_to(self.root)) if self.root in f.parents else f.name
        for i, raw in enumerate(f.read_text(errors="ignore").splitlines(), 1):
            clean = COMMENT_RE.sub("", raw)
            self.lines.append((rel, i, clean, raw))
            for m in INPUT_RE.finditer(clean):
                tgt = m.group(1).strip()
                for cand in (self.base / tgt, self.base / (tgt + ".tex")):
                    if cand.is_file():
                        self._load(cand, seen)
                        break

    def where(self, offset):
        i = max(0, bisect.bisect_right(self.offsets, offset) - 1)
        rel, ln, _, _ = self.lines[i]
        return f"{rel}:{ln}"


def _opts(s):
    return [o.strip() for o in (s or "").split(",") if o.strip()]


def run(path, rules, names=None, main=None):
    T = rules.get("tex", {}) or {}
    S = sources(T)
    names = names or []
    F = []
    src = Source(path, main)
    F.append(Finding("tex.main", "skip", "Main file detected", f"{src.main.name} (+{len(src.lines)} source lines)"))

    # ---- documentclass ------------------------------------------------
    DC = T.get("documentclass")
    if DC:
        m = DOCCLASS_RE.search(src.clean)
        if not m:
            F.append(finding("tex.documentclass", False, "\\documentclass found", "No \\documentclass in the source"))
        else:
            opts, name = _opts(m.group(1)), m.group(2).strip()
            probs = []
            if DC.get("name") and name != DC["name"]:
                probs.append(f"class is '{name}', expected '{DC['name']}'")
            probs += [f"missing option '{o}'" for o in DC.get("options_required", []) if o not in opts]
            probs += [f"forbidden option '{o}'" for o in DC.get("options_forbidden", []) if o in opts]
            want = f"\\documentclass[{','.join(DC.get('options_required', []))}]{{{DC.get('name', name)}}}"
            F.append(finding("tex.documentclass", not probs, "\\documentclass matches the template",
                             "; ".join(probs), location=src.where(m.start()),
                             fix=f"Use: {want}", source=S.get("documentclass", "")))

    # ---- packages -----------------------------------------------------
    used = {}   # name -> (options, location)
    for m in USEPKG_RE.finditer(src.clean):
        for pk in _opts(m.group(2)):
            used[pk] = (_opts(m.group(1)), src.where(m.start()))
    for req in T.get("packages_required", []):
        req = {"name": req} if isinstance(req, str) else req
        nm = req["name"]
        if nm not in used:
            F.append(finding(f"tex.pkg.{nm}", False, f"Required package '{nm}' is loaded",
                             f"\\usepackage{{{nm}}} not found",
                             fix="Add `\\usepackage" + (f"[{','.join(req['options_required'])}]" if req.get("options_required") else "") + f"{{{nm}}}`",
                             source=S.get("packages_required", "")))
            continue
        o, loc = used[nm]
        probs = [f"missing option '{x}'" for x in req.get("options_required", []) if x not in o]
        probs += [f"forbidden option '{x}'" for x in req.get("options_forbidden", []) if x in o]
        F.append(finding(f"tex.pkg.{nm}", not probs, f"Package '{nm}' loaded with the right options",
                         "; ".join(probs), location=loc,
                         fix=f"Use `\\usepackage[{','.join(req.get('options_required', []))}]{{{nm}}}`",
                         source=S.get("packages_required", "")))
    forb = T.get("packages_forbidden")
    if forb is None and T.get("forbid_layout_hacks", False):
        forb = DEFAULT_FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES
    allow = set(T.get("allow_packages", []))
    bad = []
    for pk in forb or []:
        pk, why = (pk["name"], pk.get("reason", "")) if isinstance(pk, dict) else (pk, "")
        if pk in used and pk not in allow:
            bad.append(f"{pk} ({used[pk][1]}){': ' + why if why else ''}")
    if forb is not None:
        F.append(finding("tex.pkg_forbidden", not bad, "No forbidden layout packages", "; ".join(bad),
                         fix="Remove these `\\usepackage` lines. They change margins/spacing and often trigger desk rejection.",
                         source=S.get("packages_forbidden", S.get("forbid_layout_hacks", "")), severity=T.get("layout_hacks_severity", "error")))

    # ---- layout hacks -------------------------------------------------
    if T.get("forbid_layout_hacks", False):
        hits = []
        for rel, ln, clean, _ in src.lines:
            for rx, label, fix in LAYOUT_HACKS:
                if re.search(rx, clean):
                    hits.append((f"{rel}:{ln}", label, fix, clean.strip()[:70]))
        F.append(finding("tex.layout_hacks", not hits, "No spacing/margin hacks in the source",
                         "" if not hits else f"{len(hits)} hit(s): " + "; ".join(f"{l} {lab} `{c}`" for l, lab, _, c in hits[:8]),
                         location=", ".join(h[0] for h in hits[:8]),
                         fix=" / ".join(sorted({h[2] for h in hits})[:3]),
                         source=S.get("forbid_layout_hacks", ""),
                         severity=T.get("layout_hacks_severity", "warn")))

    # ---- bibliography style -----------------------------------------
    bs_allowed = T.get("bibliography_style")
    if bs_allowed:
        m = re.search(r"\\bibliographystyle\s*\{([^}]*)\}", src.clean)
        if not m and not re.search(r"\\bibliography\s*\{", src.clean):
            F.append(Finding("tex.bibstyle", "skip", "Bibliography style is the required one",
                             "No BibTeX (\\bibliography) in the source: thebibliography/biblatex cannot be verified "
                             f"automatically. Required style: {', '.join(bs_allowed)}."))
        else:
            F.append(finding("tex.bibstyle", bool(m) and m.group(1).strip() in bs_allowed,
                             "Bibliography style is the required one",
                             f"found '{m.group(1)}'" if m else "\\bibliography used but no \\bibliographystyle",
                             location=src.where(m.start()) if m else "",
                             fix=f"Use `\\bibliographystyle{{{bs_allowed[0]}}}` and the official .bst file.",
                             source=S.get("bibliography_style", "")))

    # ---- official style files untouched ------------------------------
    off = T.get("official_files") or {}
    if off:
        assets = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "assets" / "official"
        for fname, meta in off.items():
            found = [f for f in src.root.rglob(fname)]
            if not found:
                F.append(Finding(f"tex.official.{fname}", "skip", f"Official file {fname} untouched",
                                 "not in the project folder (maybe loaded from the TeX tree) - cannot verify"))
                continue
            if not meta.get("sha256"):
                F.append(Finding(f"tex.official.{fname}", "skip", f"Official file {fname} untouched", "no reference hash in rules.json (rebuild the skill with --inventory)"))
                continue
            h = sha256_normalized(found[0])
            same = h == meta["sha256"]
            diff = ""
            ref = assets / fname
            if not same and ref.exists():
                d = list(difflib.unified_diff(ref.read_text(errors="ignore").splitlines(),
                                              found[0].read_text(errors="ignore").splitlines(),
                                              "official", "yours", n=0, lineterm=""))
                diff = " | ".join(d[:10])
            F.append(finding(f"tex.official.{fname}", same, f"Official file {fname} is unmodified",
                             "" if same else "Differs from the kit version. " + diff,
                             location=str(found[0].relative_to(src.root)),
                             fix=f"Replace it with the original {fname} from the author kit and move any customisation "
                                 "into your own .tex file (if the venue allows it).",
                             source=S.get("official_files", "")))

    # ---- anonymity ----------------------------------------------------
    A = rules.get("anonymity") or {}
    if A.get("required"):
        leaks = []
        for nm in names:
            for rel, ln, clean, raw in src.lines:
                if nm and nm.lower() in raw.lower():
                    leaks.append(f"{rel}:{ln} contains '{nm}'" + ("" if nm.lower() in clean.lower() else " (inside a comment)"))
        for rel, ln, clean, raw in src.lines:
            if EMAIL_RE.search(raw):
                leaks.append(f"{rel}:{ln} email address")
            for pat in A.get("forbid_text_patterns", []):
                if re.search(pat, clean, re.I):
                    leaks.append(f"{rel}:{ln} matches /{pat}/")
        for m in re.finditer(r"\\(?:thanks|affiliation|email)\s*\{", src.clean):
            leaks.append(f"{src.where(m.start())} \\{m.group(0)[1:-1].strip()} (check it is hidden in review mode)")
        F.append(finding("tex.anon", not leaks, "No identifying information in the source",
                         "" if not leaks else "; ".join(leaks[:10]),
                         fix="Blank the author block (the template's review mode usually does this), delete emails, "
                             "acknowledgements and self-identifying links; strip comments that name people.",
                         source=sources(A).get("required", ""), severity="error"))
    return F, src


# ---- helpers used by the checklist evaluator ------------------------------------
def section_words(src, title_regex):
    """Return (found, words) for the first section whose title matches. Approximate."""
    head = re.compile(r"\\(?:sub)*section\*?\s*\{([^}]*)\}")
    ms = list(head.finditer(src.clean))
    for i, m in enumerate(ms):
        if re.fullmatch(title_regex, m.group(1).strip(), re.I):
            end = ms[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(ms) else len(src.clean)
            body = src.clean[m.end():end]
            body = re.sub(r"\\(cite[a-z]*|ref|label|eqref)\s*(\[[^\]]*\])?\{[^}]*\}", " ", body)
            body = re.sub(r"\\[a-zA-Z]+\*?", " ", body)
            return True, len(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]{3,}", body)), src.where(m.start())
    return False, 0, ""

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Venue format checker.

  python scripts/run_checks.py --rules rules.json --pdf paper.pdf --tex paper_dir_or.zip \
      [--docx paper.docx [--docx-to-pdf]] [--phase review|final] [--names "Wei Feng,Jai Lee"] \
      [--out report.md] [--json report.json]

The rules file is data; this engine is generic. Findings carry the kit source of the rule and a concrete fix.
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

# Reports include Unicode symbols and manuscript text even on Windows pipes.
for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
    if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure"):
        stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from checks.common import Finding, deep_merge  # noqa: E402


def evaluate_checklist(items, pdf_ctx, tex_src):
    from checks import check_tex
    out = []
    for it in items:
        dets = it.get("detect") or []
        if isinstance(dets, dict):
            dets = [dets]
        sev = it.get("severity", "error")
        res = None
        for d in dets:
            t = d.get("type")
            if t == "tex_regex" and tex_src is not None:
                found = any(re.search(p, tex_src.clean, re.I | re.M) for p in d["patterns"])
                res = (found == (d.get("expect", "present") == "present"),
                       "found in LaTeX source" if found else "not found in LaTeX source", "")
            elif t == "tex_section" and tex_src is not None:
                ok, words, loc = check_tex.section_words(tex_src, d["title_regex"])
                need = d.get("min_words", 1)
                res = (ok and words >= need,
                       (f"section found ({loc}), about {words} words" if ok else "section not found") +
                       (f"; expected at least {need}" if ok and words < need else ""), loc)
            elif t == "pdf_regex" and pdf_ctx is not None:
                found = any(re.search(p, pdf_ctx["text"], re.I | re.M) for p in d["patterns"])
                res = (found == (d.get("expect", "present") == "present"),
                       "found in PDF text" if found else "not found in PDF text", "")
            if res is not None:
                break
        title = it.get("title", it["id"])
        fix = it.get("fix", "")
        if res is None:
            out.append(Finding(f"checklist.{it['id']}", "manual", title,
                               it.get("description", "") + " (cannot be detected automatically with the given inputs)",
                               fix=fix, source=it.get("source", "")))
        else:
            ok, detail, loc = res
            if ok and it.get("needs_judgement"):
                out.append(Finding(f"checklist.{it['id']}", "manual", title,
                                   "Auto-detected: " + detail + ". Content still needs a human/LLM judgement: "
                                   + it.get("description", ""), location=loc, fix=fix, source=it.get("source", "")))
            else:
                st = "pass" if ok else ("fail" if sev == "error" else "warn")
                out.append(Finding(f"checklist.{it['id']}", st, title, detail, location=loc, fix=fix,
                                   source=it.get("source", "")))
    return out


def render(venue, phase, findings, inputs):
    c = Counter(f.status for f in findings)
    L = [f"# Format check: {venue}" + (f" ({phase})" if phase else ""), "",
         "Inputs: " + ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in inputs.items() if v), "",
         f"**{c['fail']} must fix**, {c['warn']} warnings, {c['manual']} manual checks, "
         f"{c['pass']} passed, {c['skip']} not checked.", ""]

    def block(title, status, icon):
        items = [f for f in findings if f.status == status]
        if not items:
            return
        L.append(f"## {icon} {title}")
        for f in items:
            L.append(f"### {f.title}  `{f.id}`")
            if f.detail:
                L.append(f"- Problem: {f.detail}")
            if f.location:
                L.append(f"- Where: {f.location}")
            if f.fix:
                L.append(f"- Fix: {f.fix}")
            if f.source:
                L.append(f"- Rule source: {f.source}")
            L.append("")

    block("Must fix", "fail", "❌")
    block("Warnings", "warn", "⚠️")
    block("Manual checks", "manual", "✋")
    passed = [f for f in findings if f.status == "pass"]
    if passed:
        L.append("## ✅ Passed")
        L += [f"- {f.title}" + (f" ({f.detail})" if f.detail else "") for f in passed] + [""]
    skipped = [f for f in findings if f.status == "skip"]
    if skipped:
        L.append("## ⏭️ Not checked")
        L += [f"- {f.title}: {f.detail}" for f in skipped] + [""]
    return "\n".join(L)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--rules", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "rules.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--pdf")
    ap.add_argument("--tex")
    ap.add_argument("--docx")
    ap.add_argument("--project", help="whole paper folder: finds main .tex and the paper PDF (or compiles a copy), checks figures and the folder")
    ap.add_argument("--main", help="main .tex relative to --project/--tex when several files have \\documentclass")
    ap.add_argument("--no-compile", action="store_true", help="do not compile when the folder has no paper PDF")
    ap.add_argument("--docx-to-pdf", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--phase")
    ap.add_argument("--names", default="", help="comma-separated author/institution names to search for (anonymity)")
    ap.add_argument("--out")
    ap.add_argument("--json")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    rules = json.load(open(a.rules, encoding="utf-8"))
    phase = a.phase or rules.get("default_phase")
    if phase and (rules.get("phases") or {}).get(phase):
        rules = deep_merge(rules, rules["phases"][phase])
    names = [n.strip() for n in a.names.split(",") if n.strip()]

    if a.project and a.project.lower().endswith(".zip"):
        import zipfile
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="project_")
        zipfile.ZipFile(a.project).extractall(d)
        top = [p for p in Path(d).iterdir() if p.name != "__MACOSX"]
        a.project = str(top[0]) if len(top) == 1 and top[0].is_dir() else d
    if a.project:
        a.tex = a.tex or a.project
    if not (a.pdf or a.tex or a.docx):
        ap.error("give at least one of --project / --pdf / --tex / --docx")

    F, pdf_ctx, tex_src = [], None, None
    if a.docx:
        from checks import check_docx
        f, dctx = check_docx.run(a.docx, rules, names)
        F += f
        if a.docx_to_pdf and not a.pdf:
            exe = shutil.which("soffice") or shutil.which("libreoffice")
            if exe:
                tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
                subprocess.run([exe, "--headless", "--convert-to", "pdf", "--outdir", tmp, a.docx],
                               capture_output=True, timeout=180)
                pdfs = list(Path(tmp).glob("*.pdf"))
                if pdfs:
                    a.pdf = str(pdfs[0])
            else:
                F.append(Finding("docx.to_pdf", "skip", "DOCX -> PDF conversion", "LibreOffice not available"))
    if a.tex:
        from checks import check_tex
        f, tex_src = check_tex.run(a.tex, rules, names, a.main)
        F += f
    compiled = False
    if a.project and tex_src is not None:
        from checks import check_project
        root = Path(a.project)
        how = "given on the command line" if a.pdf else "none"
        if not a.pdf:
            pdf, others = check_project.find_paper_pdf(root, tex_src)
            if pdf:
                a.pdf, how = str(pdf), "found in the folder" + (f" (ignored other PDFs: {', '.join(o.name for o in others[:4])})" if others else "")
            elif not a.no_compile:
                pdf, log = check_project.compile_project(root, tex_src.main)
                if pdf:
                    a.pdf, compiled, how = str(pdf), True, "compiled from a copy of the project"
                else:
                    F.append(Finding("proj.compile", "fail", "The project compiles",
                                     "Compilation failed. Log tail: " + " ".join(log.split())[-600:],
                                     fix="Fix the first error in the log (usually a missing package, a missing figure or a style file not in the folder). "
                                         "A paper that does not compile cannot be submitted."))
            else:
                how = "none (compilation disabled)"
        F.append(Finding("proj.inputs", "skip", "Project inputs",
                         f"main source: {tex_src.main.name}; paper PDF: {Path(a.pdf).name if a.pdf else 'none'} ({how})"))
    if a.pdf:
        from checks import check_pdf
        f, pdf_ctx = check_pdf.run(a.pdf, rules, names)
        F += f
    if a.project and tex_src is not None:
        from checks import check_project
        F += check_project.run(a.project, tex_src, a.pdf, rules, names, compiled)
    F += evaluate_checklist(rules.get("checklist", []), pdf_ctx, tex_src)

    if not a.pdf:
        F.append(Finding("pdf.missing", "skip", "Compiled-PDF checks (page count, margins, fonts)",
                         "No PDF provided. Compile the paper and pass --pdf: these are the checks that decide desk rejection."))
    if not a.tex and not a.docx:
        F.append(Finding("src.missing", "skip", "Source checks (packages, style file integrity, layout hacks)",
                         "No LaTeX source provided; only the PDF was inspected."))

    rep = render(rules.get("venue", "venue"), phase, F, {"pdf": a.pdf, "tex": a.tex, "docx": a.docx})
    if a.out:
        Path(a.out).write_text(rep, encoding="utf-8")
    if a.json:
        Path(a.json).write_text(json.dumps([f.to_dict() for f in F], ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(rep)
    sys.exit(1 if any(f.status == "fail" for f in F) else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Venue checker factory

Builds a per-venue format-check skill from an author kit. The factory contains a generic, tested checking engine; what it produces for each
venue is mostly **data** (`rules.json` extracted from the kit, with a source pointer for every rule) plus the kit's official style files
(so the engine can detect a modified style file by hash). Keeping rules as data is what makes the result checkable and cheap to update when the venue
revises its kit.

Do not hand-write a venue's checking code. If the engine lacks a check the kit needs, either express it as a `checklist` item (regex or manual) or
extend `scripts/checks/` and re-run the self-test, so every generated skill benefits.

## Workflow

### 1. Pin down the target
Ask only what you cannot read from the kit: venue + year, **track** (long/short/demo/journal article type), and which **phase** the user will mostly
check (review / camera-ready; model both when the kit covers both). Ask for the full kit: formatting-instructions PDF, template folder or zip
(.tex/.sty/.cls/.bst), CFP page, and any checklist. If the user only names the venue and fetching is possible, look for the official kit
and say which pages you used. The official source, not memory, is what the rules come from.

### 2. Extract the kit
```
python scripts/extract_kit.py <uploaded files or dirs> --out /home/claude/work/kit_text
```
Then read, in this order: `inventory.json` (what is in the kit, hashes), the formatting-instructions text, `style_digest.md` (the .sty/.cls is the
ground truth for geometry, fonts and review/final options), then the CFP and any checklist. Read the text itself; do not skim a summary. Kits bury hard rules
in footnotes ("papers that violate the margin will be rejected", "Type 3 fonts are not allowed").

### 3. Interview the user about what the kit leaves open, then write `rules.json`
Same habit as skill-creator's interview step: do not guess where the kit is vague. While reading, keep a list of open points and ask the user
(one batch, at most three questions, with concrete options, e.g. via `ask_user_input_v0` when available) before finalizing. Typical ones: which
track / paper type; whether review and camera-ready should both be modelled; which "should" items to treat as errors; whether sections the kit
does not mention (appendix, ethics) count toward the limit; how strict to be on spacing tweaks. Record each answer in `_sources` as
"user decision", so it is distinguishable from what the kit says.

Follow `references/rules-schema.md` (read it now; it has the full schema, a kit-wording-to-rule table, and traps). Principles:
- Only encode what the kit states. Silence means no rule. Do not backfill from what other venues usually require.
- Every rule gets a `_sources` entry or a checklist `source` with file/page and a few words of the original, because the user will verify them.
- Mark severity from the kit's language: "must / will be rejected" is `error`; "should / encouraged" is `warn`.
- Model phases (review vs final) as overrides, and put tracks in separate skills or ask.
- Requirements that cannot be machine-checked (novelty statements, ethics content, checklist answers) become manual checklist items with a precise description of
  what to verify, never silently dropped.
- Compute derived values (text block -> margins) yourself and say so in `_sources`.

### 4. Build the venue skill
```
python scripts/build_venue_skill.py --name <venue>-<year>-format-check --rules rules.json \
    --inventory kit_text/inventory.json --kit-notes kit_notes.md --out /home/claude/skills
```
`kit_notes.md` is a short human-readable digest you write: the rules table (rule, value, source), judgement calls you made, conflicts between kit documents,
and what is **not** covered. The builder lints the rules (missing sources, incomplete margins, empty heading list), copies the engine, hashes and copies the official
style files, and writes the venue `SKILL.md`. Fix every WARNING it prints.

### 5. Calibrate before trusting it (do not skip)
A checker with false alarms gets ignored; one with false passes is worse. Test it on the kit itself:
1. **Positive control.** Compile the kit's own sample paper (needs the kit's style files; `pdflatex` + `bibtex`). In the review phase the engine should report
   **zero must-fix**. Every must-fix on the official sample is a wrong rule or a wrong engine assumption: fix the rule (or the engine) and re-run.
2. **Negative controls.** Make 3-5 mutated copies, each breaking one thing: add `\vspace{-1cm}`, switch the font/size, put an author name in the review version,
   delete the Limitations section, overflow a table, edit one line of the .sty. Each must be caught with a fix that points at the right place.
3. If the kit has no sample, build a small synthetic paper with the kit's style and do the same, and tell the user the positive control is weaker.
Report what you tested and what failed along the way. If something could not be tested (e.g. no style files in the kit), say so plainly.

### 6. Show the user the rules, then deliver
Present a compact table of the extracted rules with sources and mark the ones you are least sure of (derived values, ambiguous wording, conflicts), and ask
them to confirm or correct before relying on it. Then package:
```
cd /mnt/skills/examples/skill-creator && python -m scripts.package_skill /home/claude/skills/<name> /mnt/user-data/outputs
```
and share the `.skill` file with `present_files`. Tell the user how to use it next time (upload paper + say the venue/phase), and that for a new venue they
upload that venue's kit and invoke this factory again.

## Notes on the engine (what generated skills can do)
- **Project mode** (`--project folder-or-zip`): the user is expected to upload the whole paper folder. It finds the main .tex, picks the paper PDF among
  figure PDFs, compiles a copy when no PDF exists, flags a stale PDF, checks each included figure (exists, fonts), and scans the folder for identity leaks.
  Positive/negative controls in step 5 should therefore be run in project mode on a folder, not only on a loose PDF.
- PDF: page size, main-body page limit (heading-based), margins (words + images), allowed fonts, body/min font size, embedded and Type 3 fonts, line numbers,
  metadata and text anonymity (emails, code-hosting links, names the user supplies, Acknowledgements).
- LaTeX: documentclass/package options, forbidden packages, layout hacks (negative vspace, geometry, linespread, length overrides), bibliography style,
  **modified official style files** (hash + diff), anonymity leaks including comments, checklist sections by regex or section word count.
- Word: page size, margins, fonts, body size, line spacing; page count via PDF export.
- Output: markdown report + JSON, each finding with location, concrete fix and the kit source of the rule.
- Not covered: anything inside vector figures, semantic requirements (is the ethics statement adequate), submission-system-specific checks. State this to the user.
